video.title: The Players To NOT DRAFT This Fantasy Basketball Season

summary: Josh Lloyd runs through a "do not draft" list, round by round from round 1 to round 10, using the current Yahoo and ESPN rankings for category and points leagues. He says "do not draft" only means the player is ranked too high at his current spot, not that he has no value. He spends a long stretch criticizing ESPN's updated category rankings, calling them careless, and tells listeners to move their leagues to other platforms. Main targets include ESPN's early picks of Deni Avdija, Bam Adebayo, Devin Booker, Josh Giddey and Ty Jerome, plus Yahoo's Tyrese Haliburton at 10, Trae Young, Donovan Mitchell, Jalen Brunson in category leagues, Walker Kessler, Alex Sarr and Brandon Ingram. A recurring theme is that combined Yahoo rankings mix formats, so players who are good in points leagues get overrated for categories, and the reverse.

rules.text: A do not draft label means the player is ranked too high at his current spot. Everyone has value at the right price, so taking him a round or two later is fine.
rules.quote: It just means where they're currently positioned, you would be doing it wrong in my opinion to take them there.

rules.text: Yahoo rankings blend several people's opinions and every format, so they can misrank players for a specific format. Check category and points value separately.
rules.quote: there are mushed combined consensus between multiple people's opinions but also every format under the sun.

rules.text: Players who score well and get to the line, like volume-scoring guards, can be much better in points leagues than in category leagues.
rules.quote: He's not worth a third round pick in a category. If you're in a points league, mate, knock yourself out.

rules.text: Do not pay for a player expecting big stat jumps from a small sample (about five games) to carry over to a full season.
rules.quote: I'm not going to risk that on absolute best case randomness from five games carrying over to 70.

rules.text: Rankings that lean on season totals from players who play every game can overrate weak per-game producers.
rules.quote: It's overindexing on the totals. He is no not even close to being that good as a

rules.text: Players coming back from injury often face minutes limits and rest days early in the season, which cuts their full-season value.
rules.quote: I just think for a month or two, there'll be some restrictions, which over the course of the season limits

rules.text: A player on a bad team who could be traded to a better team carries risk. A usage drop after a trade can wreck his value right when fantasy playoffs start.
rules.quote: if he is traded, it's probably to a better team. Meaning when you hit tier fantasy playoffs, if Norm Pal

rules.text: Rebuilding teams that do not control their own draft pick may still give minutes to young players instead of veterans.
rules.quote: the team doesn't have control of their draft pick so they prioritize developing Yakonis and Burries and Rollins

rules.text: Rookies are often overvalued. Their games may not translate right away, so avoid paying a high price unless the rookie is truly NBA ready. Being an older rookie does not make a player NBA ready.
rules.quote: Just cuz you're old doesn't mean you're good.

rules.text: Around round 9 you are drafting your second-worst starter. Flyer picks start to make sense from round 10 and fit round 11 better.
rules.quote: round nine, we're theoretically targeting our second worst starter.

rules.text: Players who need injuries ahead of them to get a role are deep-league stash options. They are not mid-round picks in standard leagues.
rules.quote: If you're in a stashable format, a deeper format, you want to just hold someone in case they get hurt, go for it.

rules.text: In Yahoo points scoring, assists are worth only 1.5 points, so assist-only players have limited points league value.
rules.quote: Assists don't count that much. One and a half points on Yahoo.

rules.text: When ranking a team's players, make sure the minutes add up. If several players are ranked as 30-minute starters, a bench guard's projected role may not exist.
rules.quote: so you're suggesting that all of those guys are going to be playing 30 plus minutes. How does Gillespie do it?

rules.text: The speaker considers ESPN a poorly maintained fantasy platform: slow to add players to its database, misleading roster percentages and careless rankings. He suggests moving leagues to Fantrax, CBS, Yahoo or other sites.
rules.quote: It happens every single year where you can't add guys cuz they take three weeks to add them in.
